subject: Post-call: BlueWave connectivity & tooling onramp — SDK auth, routing, mTLS
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@bluewave.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@bluewave.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: BlueWave connectivity & tooling onramp — SDK auth, routing, mTLS

Alex / Priya — thanks for the time earlier. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Summary of goals from today
- PoC to validate private connectivity + low-latency inference for search/rerank (embeddings + light reranker).
- SDK integration for structured output / tool-calling (Node + Python initially).
- Security: mTLS preferred, support for VPC endpoint or IP allowlist as backup; audit logs/KMS requirements noted.

Technical items we said we’d follow up on
1) Networking options: AWS PrivateLink (regional VPC endpoint) vs IP allowlist. If PrivateLink: we provide the service endpoint DNS and cert bundle for mTLS; if IP allowlist: we’ll publish stable egress ranges and a maintenance notice window for changes.
2) Auth: API key short-lived tokens + optional mutual TLS for the private endpoint. We can also support customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest in Private deployments — will confirm applicability for Hosted Dedicated.
3) SDK & structured output: we’ll share example SDK snippets showing tool-calling schema (JSON schema + example reranker call) and a short sample for embeddings -> local reranker + Redwood embeddings storage.
4) Routing & failover: propose a canary route policy that sends 10% traffic to a lower-cost variant during early rollout; fallback to hosted variant if PrivateLink degrades.

Attachments: onramp_checklist.pdf (high-level checklist) attached.

Immediate asks / next steps
- BlueWave: confirm preferred networking approach (PrivateLink vs allowlist) + timeline for network team (answer by EOD Wed 4/14).
- Redwood (SE + Infra): Priyom and Vivek to prepare a 60-min technical workshop and a one-page PrivateLink connectivity guide by 4/14.
- Schedule: propose Mon 4/18 or Tue 4/19 for the workshop — please share availability.

Thanks — Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--

Subject: Re: Post-call: BlueWave connectivity & tooling onramp — SDK auth, routing, mTLS

Thanks Sean — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Networking preference: PrivateLink (AWS) is our first choice for the PoC. We want to avoid public IP allowlists unless PrivateLink proves infeasible.
- mTLS: yes, mTLS to your service endpoint is required for the PoC. We will share our client certs and expected CA chain.
- KMS / audit: we are on a managed KMS and need proof that audit logs capture inference request metadata (time, model variant, request id). Can you confirm what fields are captured?
- Timeline: aiming to have networking done and PoC ready by EOM (Apr 30). Our infra lead (Priya) will coordinate the networking side.

Also can you drop a small code example for the structured output tool-calling pattern? That will help our engineers decide on the schema. Attaching our network inventory for reference.

Alex
Alex Carter
Platform Engineer, BlueWave Analytics

Subject: Re: Post-call: BlueWave connectivity & tooling onramp — SDK auth, routing, mTLS

Alex / Priya — Priyom from Redwood SE team here, following up with the concrete options and a couple of sample snippets.

Networking options (short):
- Recommended: AWS PrivateLink (Private IPv4) with mTLS. We’ll provide a regional service name (vpce-*.amazonaws.com) and a cert bundle to validate the server. You will present your client cert during the TLS handshake. This avoids public egress and keeps route tables simple.
- Fallback: IP allowlist. If you must use this, we will publish a static set of egress ranges with a 30-day notice for changes and a maintenance SLA window for planned updates.

Auth & audit:
- Primary auth: short-lived API tokens minted by Redwood (we can integrate with your IdP for SCIM if you’d like).
- mTLS: mutual certificate validation to the PrivateLink endpoint.
- Audit logs: we capture request id, timestamp, model name + variant, route policy id, and token id. We do not capture input prompt text in plaintext in audit logs by default; we can provide filtered request metadata and a secure log export if needed for compliance reviews.

Structured output + tool-calling (snippet references):
- Quick example: structured JSON schema for tool actions + validation — link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/sdk-structured-output#example-json
- Embeddings + rerank: recommended pattern is to compute embeddings via Redwood embeddings endpoint, store locally in your vector store (e.g., Pinecone, Milvus), then call a lightweight Reranker (neural or lexical) hosted by you for final ordering; we provide a re-rank wrapper in our SDK to streamline scoring.

Attachments: sdk_snippets.zip (contains Node/Python examples for mTLS connection + structured-output examples).

Proposed workshop agenda (60 min):
- 0-10m: introductions + goals
- 10-25m: networking & PrivateLink setup (VPC, route, DNS)
- 25-40m: auth + mTLS handshake demo with sample certs
- 40-55m: SDK demo (tool-calling, embeddings flow, reranker pattern)
- 55-60m: action items + timeline

Availability: I’m open Tue 4/19 10-12 PT or Wed 4/20 09-11 PT. Sean / Vivek — can you confirm preferred slot?

— Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
--
[Attachment: sdk_snippets.zip (72KB)]

Thanks Priyom — that all looks reasonable. A few quick follow-ups:

- If we end up using IP allowlist as a temporary fallback, please send the current set of egress IP ranges and the cadence for change notifications.
- For audit logs: can you share a sample export schema (fields + example row) so our compliance team can review?
- Canary plan: we’d like a short canary that exercises both inference and rerank flows for a small percentage of live traffic (5-10%). Can you draft a 1-page canary playbook we can review during the workshop?

We’re aiming to lock the workshop for Tue 4/19 10:30 PT — Priya and I are available. If that works, please send a calendar invite and any pre-reads.

Alex
